I was recommended by a friend to check out Ninja Scroll a while back, and with the lockdown going on, I had a chance to do so. Here's a brief review for anyone interested. Coincidentally, the plot of the film involves a quarantined area for an epidemic, which is why I'm writing this.

Just for some context, Ninja Scroll received considerable acclaim following its release in 1993. Additionally, the Wachowskis stated it was in influence for them in making the Matrix.

Ninja Scroll follows a wandering ninja during the Edo period who stumbles upon a conspiracy surrounding an epidemic involving demonic warriors whom he must eventually battle.

The animation is good enough for its time. The faces of the characters are not your typical anime style, but you get used to it fairly quickly.

The music and sound effects are nothing special. I watched the English dub, which was fine, though not outstanding.

The real star of the movie are the fight scenes. Well animated and cleverly done. What really shines are the demons themselves, who all have unique and interesting abilities that make the fights really challenging. Some of these fights are pretty memorable.

It's a fairly mature anime, with plenty of blood and lot of sexual themes as well. The story is OK, nothing super special, but the characters are decent. It can be a little difficult to follow at times, but really the story is just there to take you from one fight to another.

Overall, it's a good film, but not a great one. I don't necessarily see why it received that much hype. Some have compared it to Ghost in the Shell and Akira, which I find to be overhyping it. It's not that good. Also, I really don't see any influence of this film as far as the Matrix is concerned.

If you are looking for an anime film with good animation, well choreographed fights, and a dark feel, this will do.
